thread:
maria: starting a thread for the SA region GKE cluster bring-up (gke-sa1). primary goals: GPU capacity for inference validation, cost-conscious preemptible pools, and a clean handoff to platform. asking for a quick runbook + validation checklist.

lee: +1. i'm on infra. pushed a terraform module branch `gke/sa1-gpu`. created two node pools: `gpu-t4-preemptible` and `cpu-standard`. autoscaler configured. still need kube-system addons and driver daemonset.

kai: double-checking: are we doing node auto-provisioning or fixed pools? preemptible GPUs can cause pod evictions we need to handle.

maria: fixed pools for now. we want predictable labels/taints for scheduling: `gpu=true, workload=inference`. preemptible for cost on the GPU pool only.

natalie: i updated the network layout in the TF branch: private cluster, cloud NAT for egress, and firewall rules limited to internal infra CIDRs + port 22 for bastion.

lee: infra notes: machine type `n1-highmem-16` + `nvidia-tesla-t4` on GPU pool, min=0,max=6, initial=2. cpu pool `e2-standard-8`, min=2,max=8.

maria: ops checklist request: list of commands to validate cluster and a tiny gpu smoke test pod. can someone paste the short snippets?

kai: here's the quick validate block — run from CI runner with gcloud creds:

```bash
gcloud container clusters get-credentials gke-sa1 --region sa-east1 --project redwood-inference-prod
kubectl get nodes -o wide
kubectl get pods -n kube-system
```

lee: install base addons via helm (we have internal helm repo): metrics-server, coredns (node-local), calico (network policy), nvidia-device-plugin, node-problem-detector. example:

```bash
helm repo add redwood-infra https://helm.redwood.ai/charts
helm install metrics-server redwood-infra/metrics-server --namespace kube-system --set args={"--kubelet-insecure-tls"}
helm install nvidia-plugin redwood-infra/nvidia-device-plugin --namespace kube-system
```

maria: include driver install: use GKE's node GPU driver install via metadata `install-gpu-driver=true` or run the daemonset. prefer node metadata flag for managed driver.

natalie: confirmed terraform sets the node metadata flag. also enabled shielded nodes and baseline pod security policies.

kai: gpu smoke test pod YAML (simple):

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: gpu-test
  labels:
    test: gpu
spec:
  containers:
  - name: nvidia-smi
    image: nvidia/cuda:11.0-base
    resources:
      limits:
        nvidia.com/gpu: 1
    command: ["/bin/sh","-c","nvidia-smi && sleep 30"]
  restartPolicy: Never
```

maria: great. expected output: `NVIDIA-SMI` table and driver version listed. also run `kubectl describe node <gpu-node>` to check NVIDIA GPU allocatable.

lee: health checks: we run `kubectl get cs` (cluster components) and check `kubectl get pod -A | egrep -v 'Running|Completed'` to surface failed system pods.

ops-bot: [cluster-health] gke-sa1 initial probes: API reachable, control plane healthy, etcd quorum ok. (automated at 1773008120)

maria: networking validation: from a pod, curl an internal service + external egress to metadata.google.internal must be blocked. confirm NAT works and egress policies are applied.

natalie: i ran `kubectl run curl-test --image=busybox --rm -i -- /bin/sh -c 'wget -qO- http://metadata.google.internal || true'` — returned nothing as expected. NAT egress to internet works with cloud NAT.

lee: cost note: preemptible GPUs cut cost ~70% but expect frequent evicts. set PodDisruptionBudget and fallback scheduling to `cpu-standard` pool when GPU not available. autoscaler on CPU pool should scale fast (min 2 -> +).

kai: add a mutating webhook to annotate pods for GPU fallback? maybe overkill. instead add a toleration-based fallback in the app: use `nodeSelector` to prefer gpu nodes, and `initContainer` that checks for GPU presence.

maria: handoff checklist (minimal):
- terraform PR merged and state locked
- helm releases for kube-system installed and verified
- gpu smoke test passed on 2 nodes
- autoscaler configured and tested via load test
- RBAC: platform service accounts created and granted `edit` on `ml-*` namespaces
- logging/metrics forwarded to ELK and prometheus
- billing alert for region and GPU SKU created

lee: i've added prometheus scrape targets and forwarding. logs indexed into the platform `clusters-sa1-*` index. billing alert created for GPU spend > $800/day.

deploy-bot: Deployment `ml-model-eval` canary to cpu-standard pool initiated at 1773008205.

maria: final manual validations i want before handoff: run a sustained 30-min job that requests 2 GPUs and confirms model runs without OOM/driver errors. also observe preemptible evictions to ensure our retry logic works.

natalie: I'll run the 30-min canary at 09:00 UTC tomorrow and post results.

kai: few follow-ups for platform:
- add node labels to the inventory service for capacity planning
- add cluster to the centralized cost-optimizer job
- update the ops runbook with exact TF module versions and helm chart SHAs

maria: thanks all. if the canary goes green and the smoke tests are clean, i'll mark ready-for-handoff and notify platform oncall.

lee: FYI: leaving a short postmortem template in the PR in case preemptibles cause more churn than expected.

ops-bot: [cluster-health] gke-sa1 post-helm-check: all kube-system pods Running. (automated at 1773008250)

maria: excellent. tagging platform-oncall: @natalie please confirm you can accept the handoff after the canary.

natalie: will confirm after 09:30 UTC.

maria: thanks everyone. single-line summary for ops notes: "gke-sa1: GPU preemptible nodepool (t4), managed gpu drivers, base addons (metrics-server, calico, nvidia plugin), cloud NAT egress; canary scheduled; awaiting 30-min run."

lee: marking infra tasks done in the TF branch. merging after CI.

maria: closing here. will open a short follow-up thread if the canary shows any regressions. :thumbsup:
